text:
erica: Quick heads-up — found a weird KV growth mode when running qwen-13b longprefetch on long contexts (~60k). Memory climbs even with steady QPS, eviction rate spikes but we keep accumulating small "tombstone" pages. Profiling attached below.

sam: Can you repro with a minimal script? also which runtime/kernel path is used (amx/fastgemm/fallback)?

erica: Repro is pretty small: run the loadtest with prefetch_window=1024 and batch_size=4, sequence=60000, recurrent prompts. We get the steady-state KV pages rising. Kernel selector shows a fallback to the portable kernel around the same time. Snippet:```python
# repro client
for i in range(1000):
    ctx = 'A'*60000
    gen(api, prompt=ctx, max_tokens=16)
```

jon: Noted — fallback to portable kernel can change allocation pattern. When the optimized kernel handles KV streaming we do different alignment; fallback can create smaller slab allocations -> fragmentation. Did you see a spike in small allocs?

erica: yes, small alloc spike and slab fragmentation. Telemetry: KV pages 1.1M -> 2.6M in ~3h, frag_ratio ~0.38, eviction churn up 3x.

perf-bot: summary: "kv_pages: 1.12M -> 2.61M, frag_ratio:0.38, evict_ops/sec: +210% (window 15m)"

maya: Two other things to consider: 1) GQA vs MQA differences — GQA allocates per-head K/V so for same model dims GQA uses ~1.6x KV memory vs MQA. 2) rope scaling mismatch: qwen mixes rope scales in a couple of blocks for rotary variants; we observed that when rope_base != runtime_scale the KV re-use fingerprint doesn't match and we keep redundant entries.

sam: Ah — rope mismatch causing cache duplication. That'd explain tombstones: entries hashed differently so old pages can't be coalesced. How often does the prefetch window interact?

erica: Prefetch_window=1024 seems to exacerbate it. With prefetch=128 the growth is flat. So the heuristic that pulls ahead too far is exposing the duplication race.

jon: Proposed experiments: 1) force kernel selector to optimized path for qwen-13b and rerun; 2) reduce prefetch_window and add a conservative coalescer pass on eviction; 3) expose a per-model rope-normalization toggle to unify the hash.

maya: Also look at GQA vs MQA config: when we run Llama/mistral with MQA we didn't hit the same magnitude. So weight this by model attention type in the routing policy.

sam: I'm going to try (1) and (2) now on a small canary. Will post logs.

ci-bot: started job build/kv-coalescer-checkpoint-312 (canary)

sam: quick log dump: "alloc_small_count +47% at T=2h after prefetch; coalescer runs: 0"

erica: thanks. If coalescer never ran that's a bug — it should trigger when frag_ratio>0.25. Opening issue with traces and perf profile.

perf-bot: issue created: #INF-4521 (kv-coalescer: conditional not firing during prefetch-heavy workloads)

erica: Next steps: (a) short-term: lower prefetch default for qwen variants and add model-aware prefetch caps; (b) medium: ensure kernel selector stability or at least consistent allocation strategy across fallbacks; (c) longer: implement rope-normalization on the KV fingerprint to avoid duplicate entries across rope_scale variants. I'll file PRs for (a) and (c).

maya: +1 on normalization. We should also document behavior in the ops playbook (how to detect tombstone growth and run manual compaction).

sam: I'll attach the canary traces to #INF-4521 and run a follow-up with the optimized kernel forced.

erica: cool — thanks folks. If anyone sees similar behavior on Llama/Mistral please paste traces here.

jon: FYI metric to add: "kv_duplicate_keys_ratio" (count of same logical key repeated due to fingerprint mismatch) — that'll make triage easier.

perf-bot: metric proposal logged: #MET-1789

erica: updated issue with a short repro and timeline. will link PRs once created. :zap:
